newsitem.title: USA: American Airlines announces fare sale.
newsitem.headline: American Airlines announces fare sale.

text.p: American Airlines and American Eagle announced a fare sale on Saturday with discounts of up to 50 percent on regular 21-day excursion fares.

The announcement came hours after President Clinton intervened to end a pilots strike, apointing a presidential board to study the dispute and postponing a walkout of the second-largest U.S. carrier for 60 days.

"American Airlines and American Eagle flights are again operating normally and there is probably no better time to travel," Michael Gunn, American Airline's senior vice president of marketing, said in a statement.
"These special offers are designed to encourage travelers to make their travel plans on American and also to apologize to customers for the inconvenience they have experienced," he added.

American said sale prices would apply to tickets bought between now and March 3 and no advance purchase was needed. In addition to the lower prices, the airline also offered double air miles and complimentary upgrades for its frequent flyers.

Discounts averaged 50 percent on excursion fares in all American and American Eagle markets in the United States, including Canada and Hawaii, for travel through March 14, with discounts of about 45 percent for travel until May 31.
For European flights, fares would be up to 50 percent lower until May 31. Travel on weekends would be slightly more expensive than the new rate, the airline said.
American also promised discounts of 25-30 percent on weekday and weekend excursion fares to the Caribbean and the Bahamas until May 31, 1997.
